A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ThinkEdit study and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The earlier examples are retained under renumbered appendix sections in v4; no essential comparison material is missing.

before.justification: v3 reports original steering experiments, weight-editing evaluations on mathematical benchmarks, editing-rate analyses, and qualitative examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds evaluations on three non-math MMLU subjects and quantitative reasoning-behavior measurements in Appendices A.6–A.7.

M1.justification: Both versions extract long-minus-short reasoning directions, rank attention heads by their short-reasoning contributions, and orthogonalize selected output projections, using a default 4% editing rate. Added dimensional annotations clarify the existing method without changing its procedure.

E1.justification: v4 adds MMLU High School Computer Science, Formal Logic, and Professional Accounting evaluations across four retained models in Appendix A.6. These substantially broaden v3's mathematical evaluation coverage to additional knowledge and reasoning domains.

E2.justification: The original-model and Append "Wait" comparators remain in their corresponding mathematical experiments. The new non-math and behavioral tables use the existing original-model versus ThinkEdit comparison; no new comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: New Appendix A.7 evaluates correct and incorrect outputs using LaTeX equation counts and the frequency of boxed answers within the thinking trace, alongside token length. Existing experiments retain their stated samples, token budgets, model configurations, and shortest-response cutoffs.

E4.justification: Appendix A.7 adds a quantitative analysis of whether editing produces more explicit, structured reasoning across four models, supplementing the earlier qualitative examples. Existing steering, layerwise, editing-rate, and reasoning-length analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten independent runs in Section 4.4 and retain the existing uncertainty reporting. New Table 13 follows the established mean-with-plus/minus format; no new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is specified.

E6.justification: Tables 13–15 substantially extend the reported findings. New original-versus-ThinkEdit comparisons include 8B computer-science accuracy of 84.00% versus 88.90%, but 32B accounting accuracy of 84.22% versus 83.40%. Table 15 adds equation, answer-boxing, and length measurements, reporting average increases of 55.2%, 60.5%, and 48.0%. Tables 1–12 and the findings displayed in existing figures remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6) and their mathematical reasoning are retained. Explicit vector and scalar dimensions added in Sections 3.2 and 4.2 restate properties of existing quantities; no new assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims, including editing approximately 4% of heads and the headline +6.39% short-response and +3.34% overall accuracy improvements.

C2.justification: Appendix A.6 adds an interpretation of applicability beyond mathematics. Appendix A.7 extends the earlier example-based reasoning-quality discussion by interpreting equation and answer-boxing statistics as evidence of more explicit, structured thinking. The limitation concerning already verbose models is unchanged.

D1.justification: The direction-extraction recipe, existing hyperparameters, code-access link, and A100 hardware disclosure are retained. The added appendices do not supply new implementation instructions, software details, or resource-access information.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds Oikarinen et al. (2025) on evaluating neuron explanations and Li et al. (2025) on skill unlearning, with a brief discussion of the latter. Publication-year and venue updates for existing Sun et al. references concern retained works. Overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v4 adds an appendix contents list, expands Section 4.4's guide to supplementary material, and inserts two appendix sections while renumbering the retained examples. Local notation, model-name, and acknowledgement edits accompany an otherwise largely unchanged narrative.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 13–15 and a contents display, enlarges Figures 1 and 3, relocates and slightly enlarges Figure 4, and reduces Figure 5 to accommodate the contents list. All ten existing figure images are retained; the document is not broadly redesigned.

improvement.justification: The non-math evaluations test an applicability boundary absent from v3, and the behavioral measurements add evidence beyond selected examples, providing a modest gain in validation. However, Table 15's dataset aggregation is insufficiently specified, and its reported +48.0% length increase is not reconciled with Appendix A.3's retained -0.27% aggregate. This limits the interpretability of the new behavioral evidence.
